long_biography.plain_text:
Production gave Ilias Metaxas his distinct place in the family's spirits business. Trained as an oenologist in Dijon, he reorganised the entire operation to meet demand, overseeing infrastructure, tasting and blending while his brother Spyros concentrated on promotion and sales.

Their modern factory opened in 1967, carrying the family's established recipe into larger-scale production. After the company changed hands in 1989, Metaxas preserved inherited reserves from earlier generations. He later combined them with old company stocks for a limited “Three Generations” release, returning to the plant for the first time since the sale. Beyond business, he served as president of the Metaxa cancer hospital in Piraeus.

uncertainties: Ilias and Elias are standard transliteration variants of the Greek given name Ηλίας. The immutable record's Ilias spelling is retained. Some sources use Metaxa when referring to the brand or family name in Greek inflection, while Metaxas is the person's established Latin-script surname.

The common name produces several distinct living people: a young Harvard real-estate student, a United States project manager, a Brussels aviation strategist, a young Mykonos hotelier and a maritime-history writer born in 1944. The accepted identity requires the 1936 birth year, Piraeus and Athens geography, brother Spyros, Dijon oenology and the Metaxa production role together.

An academic history and directory entries use Ilias A. Metaxas, and Kathimerini identifies his father as Andreas. Greek patronymic conventions do not establish that A. is a Western-style middle name, so no middle-name proposal is made.
The source record's age of 84 on 16 February 2021 is exactly compatible with the direct interview's 1936 birth year, but no reliable source supplied the birth day or month. Those fields remain blank.

The family sold the Metaxa company in 1989. Kathimerini says Metaxas later participated in shipping, but it does not name a company, stake or scale. That activity is insufficient to classify his current principal industry or wealth relationship, so both remain Unknown.

The 1989 buyer is variously described as Grand Metropolitan or, retrospectively, Diageo; Grand Metropolitan later became part of Diageo. The biographies avoid naming the buyer and state only the well-supported change of ownership.

Metaxas remained alive and professionally active in a December 2024 direct interview, and focused searches found no later credible death report. The input's Alive status is retained without a new mortality proposal.

No exact personal LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok or personal website could be verified. Returned LinkedIn profiles belonged to younger namesakes with conflicting occupations and locations and were rejected rather than proposed.

No current personal net worth, investment portfolio or retained stake in the Metaxa brand is inferred. Current brand assets belong to the present company owner and are not treated as Ilias Metaxas's property.

Sensitive, private, political, controversy and legal material was excluded. Current vessel relationships were used only for cohort selection and identity disambiguation; neither biography contains a vessel name, specification or ownership fact.
